title: Apollo vs Lusha for HubSpot Enrichment — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Apollo vs Lusha for HubSpot Contact Enrichment
description: Apollo or Lusha for a small HubSpot team: free plans, self-serve prices, what syncs into HubSpot, and who has to connect it.
h1: Apollo vs Lusha for enriching HubSpot contacts
dek: Both tools find emails and phone numbers. They differ in how much of HubSpot they touch.
Prices and integration details come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown.

blocks.html: This is for a small team, a handful of reps, using {{link:hubspot}} as its CRM and needing better contact data: work emails, direct dials, company details. You've narrowed it to Apollo and Lusha because both have free plans and prices you can see.
If you need a full data platform with intent data and a sales contract, look at a broader roundup instead. This page is about getting good contact data into HubSpot without a big project.

Pick Apollo if you want one tool that finds contacts, runs outreach, and keeps HubSpot in sync both ways. Pick Lusha if you want a simpler tool that reveals contact details and pushes them into HubSpot without creating duplicates.
Both need an admin to connect. Check that before you start a trial.

Apollo has {{fact:apollo.free_plan}}. Basic is {{fact:apollo.basic_monthly}} and Professional is {{fact:apollo.professional_monthly}}. Keep in mind that {{fact:apollo.same_plan}}, so one power user can push the whole team up a tier, and {{fact:apollo.credits_expire}}.

Lusha has {{fact:lusha.free_plan}}. Starter is {{fact:lusha.starter_monthly}}, or {{fact:lusha.starter_annual}}. Professional is {{fact:lusha.pro_monthly}}. Credits: {{fact:lusha.credit_cost}}, so phone-heavy teams burn credits faster. Self-serve stops at a point: {{fact:lusha.team_limit}}.

sections.label: What each one does in HubSpot

blocks.html: Apollo's HubSpot integration offers {{fact:apollo.hubspot_two_way}}. Note that {{fact:apollo.hubspot_paid}}. You get {{fact:apollo.hubspot_setup_window}}.
Lusha {{fact:lusha.hubspot_push}}. It doesn't describe activity sync; it's built to get clean contact and company records into HubSpot.

So the real question is how much you want a second tool writing to HubSpot. Two-way sync is powerful, and it's also one more thing that can overwrite a field you care about. Set the mapping rules before you turn either one on.
If your team doesn't have a HubSpot admin, that's your first step, not the tool choice. Whoever owns the HubSpot account has to approve the connection either way.

faq.a: Both start free. On paid plans, Apollo Basic is {{fact:apollo.basic_monthly}} and Lusha Starter is {{fact:lusha.starter_monthly}}. Compare credits too, not only the sticker price.

faq.q: Which one syncs with HubSpot both ways?
faq.a: Apollo. Its HubSpot page describes {{fact:apollo.hubspot_two_way}}. Lusha pushes contacts and companies into HubSpot.

faq.q: Does the HubSpot integration cost extra?
faq.a: For Apollo, {{fact:apollo.hubspot_paid}}. Lusha's Free plan lists CRM integrations as included.

closing: Pick Apollo for prospecting plus two-way HubSpot sync, and Lusha for contact details pushed cleanly into HubSpot.

What reaches HubSpot.apollo: Contacts, accounts, deals, and activities, both ways.
What reaches HubSpot.lusha: Contacts and companies, with a duplicate check.
